fallback.text: A LoRa sensor 2 km from its gateway sends 20-byte packets at 868 MHz with 14 dBm through suburban clutter (path-loss exponent 3.3). Each step of the spreading factor lowers the receiver's sensitivity by about 2.5 dB but doubles the time on air. With the −2 dBi chip antenna the link needs SF12 for 10 dB of margin, and a packet then takes 1.3 s; a 5 dBi collinear antenna gains 7 dB, so SF9 already gives 11.9 dB of margin with 185 ms on air.
